# Setup

```{r setup}
library(ipumsr)
library(stringr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)

# Hide package messages and warnings in the knitted report
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

# Age groups used throughout (change them here only)
young_min = 22
young_max = 25
older_min = 30
older_max = 55

young_label = paste0(young_min, "-", young_max)
older_label = paste0(older_min, "-", older_max)
group_colors = setNames(c("skyblue", "navy"), c(young_label, older_label))
```

```{r load-data}
# IPUMS CPS (read once, used for both age groups)
ddi = read_ipums_ddi("cps_00003.xml")
cps_raw = read_ipums_micro(ddi)

# O*NET exposure scores
onet_exposures = read.csv("occ_level.csv")

# Crosswalks
crosswalk1 = read_excel("2002_2011_occupation_crosswalk.xls",
                        sheet = "2010summ", skip = 2, col_types = "text")

crosswalk2 = read_excel("soc_2010_to_2018_crosswalk.xlsx",
                        sheet = "Sorted by 2010", skip = 8, col_types = "text")
```

# Exposure lookup (built once, used for every group)

```{r exposure-lookup}
# BLS 2010 SOC <-> 2018 SOC
bls = crosswalk2
bls = transmute(bls,
                soc2010 = str_trim(`2010 SOC Code`),
                soc2018 = str_trim(`2018 SOC Code`))
bls = filter(bls, str_detect(soc2010, "^\\d\\d-\\d{4}$"))
bls = filter(bls, str_detect(soc2018, "^\\d\\d-\\d{4}$"))
bls = distinct(bls)

# Each O*NET occupation gets its 2010 SOC code(s)
onet = onet_exposures
onet = mutate(onet, soc2018 = str_sub(O.NET.SOC.Code, 1, 7))
onet = left_join(onet, bls, by = "soc2018", relationship = "many-to-many")

# Census 2010 occupation codes, with SOC prefixes for broad groups and wildcards
xw = crosswalk1
xw = transmute(xw,
               soc    = str_trim(`2010 SOC Code`),
               census = str_trim(`2010 Census Code`))
xw = filter(xw, str_detect(census, "^\\d{4}$"))
xw = filter(xw, soc != "none")
has_X = str_detect(xw$soc, "X")
xw$prefix = if_else(has_X,
                    str_remove(xw$soc, "X+$"),    # 15-113X -> 15-113
                    str_remove(xw$soc, "0+$"))    # 13-1030 -> 13-103

# 2010 SOC -> Census code (longest matching prefix wins)
find_census = function(s) {
  if (is.na(s)) return(NA_character_)
  hits = xw[startsWith(s, xw$prefix), ]
  if (nrow(hits) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  hits$census[which.max(nchar(hits$prefix))]
}
onet$census = vapply(onet$soc2010, find_census, character(1))

# One exposure value per Census code
census_exposure = filter(onet, !is.na(census))
census_exposure = group_by(census_exposure, census)
census_exposure = summarise(census_exposure,
                            dv_rating_beta = mean(dv_rating_beta, na.rm = TRUE),
                            .groups = "drop")
```

# Prepare the two age groups

```{r prepare-groups}
# Employed college graduates (bachelor's or higher) in an age range, with exposure attached
prepare_group = function(raw, age_min, age_max) {
  # Age range and bachelor's degree or higher
  out = raw[raw$AGE >= age_min & raw$AGE <= age_max & raw$EDUC >= 111, ]

  # Employed
  out = out[out$EMPSTAT == 1 | out$EMPSTAT == 10 | out$EMPSTAT == 12, ]

  # Valid occupation codes
  out = out[out$OCC != 0, ]
  out = out[out$OCC2010 != 9999, ]

  # Drop columns we don't use
  out$EDCYC = NULL
  out$EDDIPGED = NULL
  out$EDHGCGED = NULL

  # Average-month weight (12 pooled months)
  out$monthly_weight = out$WTFINL / 12

  # Exposure and occupation title
  codes = sprintf("%04d", as.integer(out$OCC2010))
  out$dv_rating_beta = census_exposure$dv_rating_beta[match(codes, census_exposure$census)]
  out$occ_title = as.character(as_factor(out$OCC2010))

  out
}

people_data      = prepare_group(cps_raw, young_min, young_max)
people_data_3055 = prepare_group(cps_raw, older_min, older_max)
```

# Question 1: What do 22-25 year old college graduates in the US do, and how exposed are their occupations?

```{r q1-table}
occ_table = group_by(people_data, OCC2010, occ_title)

occ_table = summarise(occ_table,
                      n_people        = n(),                    # raw respondent count
                      weighted_people = sum(monthly_weight),    # estimated people
                      exposure        = first(dv_rating_beta),  # same for everyone in the occupation
                      .groups = "drop")

# Weighted share of all young graduates
occ_table$share     = occ_table$weighted_people / sum(occ_table$weighted_people)
occ_table$share_pct = round(100 * occ_table$share, 1)

# Sort and keep the top 30
occ_table = arrange(occ_table, desc(weighted_people))
top30 = head(occ_table, 30)
top30$weighted_people = round(top30$weighted_people)
```

```{r q1-top30-chart, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
p = ggplot(top30, aes(x = exposure, y = reorder(occ_title, exposure))) +
  geom_col(fill = "skyblue") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Task exposure of the 30 largest occupations",
       x = "Exposure (dv_rating_beta)",
       y = NULL) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
        plot.title.position = "plot")

ggsave("top30_exposure.png", plot = p, width = 16, height = 9, dpi = 200)
p
```

## Comparing the age groups

```{r exposure-histogram-by-age}
young = data.frame(dv_rating_beta = people_data$dv_rating_beta,
                   w              = people_data$monthly_weight,
                   group          = young_label)

older = data.frame(dv_rating_beta = people_data_3055$dv_rating_beta,
                   w              = people_data_3055$monthly_weight,
                   group          = older_label)

both = rbind(young, older)
both = filter(both, !is.na(dv_rating_beta))

# Each person's weight as a share of their own group's total
both$w_share = both$w / ave(both$w, both$group, FUN = sum)

p_both = ggplot(both, aes(x = dv_rating_beta, weight = w_share, fill = group)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, boundary = 0, position = "dodge", color = "white") +

       fill = "Age group") +

ggsave("exposure_hist_by_age.png", plot = p_both, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 200)
p_both
```


Conclusions:

- Average level of exposure for 22-25: 0.4319888.
- Most people are honestly not too crazy exposed, mostly around 0 to 0.5, and even then the % is so low that like...
- The limitation of this, and of comparing it to 30-55, is that it doesn't differentiate between entry level, etc.
- That would have to do with the tasks, and that's where AEI comes in, but then how do you classify a task as being entry level or not?

# Question 2: Of that exposure, how much is observed automation-style vs. augmentation-style Claude usage?

```{r aei-read}
aei_data = read.csv("aei_claude_ai_2026-06-26.csv")
```

```{r aei-occupation-table}
# Global automation and augmentation data for each occupation (April 2026)
aei_occ = aei_data %>%
  filter(geo_id == "GLOBAL",
         category_name == "soc_occupation",
         hierarchy_level == 0,
         date_start == "2026-04-01",
         metric_id %in% c("pct",
                          "collaboration_bucket_automation_pct",
                          "collaboration_bucket_augmentation_pct",
                          "human_only_time_mean",
                          "human_with_ai_time_mean")) %>%
  select(node_name, node_external_id, metric_id, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric_id, values_from = value) %>%
  rename(usage_pct        = pct,
         automation_pct   = collaboration_bucket_automation_pct,
         augmentation_pct = collaboration_bucket_augmentation_pct,
         human_only_hours = human_only_time_mean,
         with_ai_minutes  = human_with_ai_time_mean)

aei_occ$automation_share = aei_occ$automation_pct / 100
```

```{r aei-to-census}
# Add the AEI values to the O*NET table, then average within each Census code
onet_aei = onet %>%
  left_join(aei_occ, by = c("O.NET.SOC.Code" = "node_external_id"))

onet_aei$node_name = NULL

census_aei = onet_aei %>%
  filter(!is.na(census), !is.na(automation_share)) %>%
  distinct(O.NET.SOC.Code, census, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  group_by(census) %>%
  summarise(automation_share = mean(automation_share),
            time_saved_share = mean(1 - with_ai_minutes / (human_only_hours * 60), na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r aei-attach-and-split}
# Attach to the young graduates
people_codes = sprintf("%04d", as.integer(people_data$OCC2010))
people_data$automation_share = census_aei$automation_share[match(people_codes, census_aei$census)]
people_data$time_saved_share = census_aei$time_saved_share[match(people_codes, census_aei$census)]

# Split each person's exposure into automation-style and augmentation-style parts
people_data$exposure_auto = people_data$dv_rating_beta * people_data$automation_share
people_data$exposure_aug  = people_data$dv_rating_beta * (1 - people_data$automation_share)

# Only people with both an exposure and an AEI value
has_aei = !is.na(people_data$dv_rating_beta) & !is.na(people_data$automation_share)
w = people_data$monthly_weight[has_aei]

coverage      = weighted.mean(has_aei, people_data$monthly_weight)   # share of all graduates covered
mean_exposure = weighted.mean(people_data$dv_rating_beta[has_aei], w)
mean_auto     = weighted.mean(people_data$exposure_auto[has_aei], w)
mean_aug      = weighted.mean(people_data$exposure_aug[has_aei], w)

coverage
mean_exposure
mean_auto
mean_aug
mean_auto + mean_aug       # should equal mean_exposure
mean_auto / mean_exposure  # share of exposure that is automation-style
```

```{r final-table}
final_table = people_data %>%
  group_by(OCC2010, occ_title) %>%
  summarise(n_people         = n(),
            weighted_people  = sum(monthly_weight),
            exposure         = first(dv_rating_beta),
            automation_share = first(automation_share),
            exposure_auto    = first(exposure_auto),
            exposure_aug     = first(exposure_aug),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(weighted_people))

final_table$share_pct = round(100 * final_table$weighted_people / sum(final_table$weighted_people), 1)

top30_final = head(final_table, 30)
top30_final
```

## Robustness check: task-weighted automation share

```{r task-ratings}
task_ratings = read_xlsx("Task Ratings.xlsx", sheet = "Task Ratings")

# Importance rating of each task within each occupation
task_imp = task_ratings %>%
  filter(`Scale ID` == "IM") %>%
  transmute(onet_code  = `O*NET-SOC Code`,
            task_id    = as.character(`Task ID`),
            importance = as.numeric(`Data Value`))

# AEI automation share for each task
aei_task = aei_data %>%
  filter(geo_id == "GLOBAL",
         category_name == "onet",
         hierarchy_level == 0,
         date_start == "2026-04-01",
         metric_id == "collaboration_bucket_automation_pct") %>%
  transmute(task_id          = as.character(node_external_id),
            automation_share = value / 100)

# Importance and automation share together (only ~9.7% of tasks have AEI data)
task_imp = left_join(task_imp, aei_task, by = "task_id")
```

```{r task-weighted-loop}
occ_codes = unique(task_imp$onet_code)

results = data.frame(onet_code             = occ_codes,
                     automation_share_task = NA_real_,
                     n_tasks               = NA_integer_,
                     n_tasks_aei           = NA_integer_,
                     importance_covered    = NA_real_)

for (i in seq_along(occ_codes)) {
  this_occ = task_imp[task_imp$onet_code == occ_codes[i], ]
  has_data = !is.na(this_occ$automation_share)

  results$n_tasks[i]            = nrow(this_occ)
  results$n_tasks_aei[i]        = sum(has_data)
  results$importance_covered[i] = sum(this_occ$importance[has_data]) / sum(this_occ$importance)

  if (sum(has_data) > 0) {
    results$automation_share_task[i] = weighted.mean(this_occ$automation_share[has_data],
                                                     this_occ$importance[has_data])
  }
}

# Add the occupation titles
results = results %>%
  left_join(select(onet_exposures, O.NET.SOC.Code, Title),
            by = c("onet_code" = "O.NET.SOC.Code")) %>%
  relocate(Title, .after = onet_code)

sum(is.na(results$Title))    # occupations with no title
```

```{r task-vs-simple}
# Compare with the simple (usage-weighted) automation share
task_compare = results %>%
  left_join(aei_occ %>% transmute(onet_code               = node_external_id,
                                  automation_share_simple = automation_share),
            by = "onet_code")

# All occupations
cor(task_compare$automation_share_task, task_compare$automation_share_simple, use = "complete.obs")
mean(abs(task_compare$automation_share_task - task_compare$automation_share_simple), na.rm = TRUE)
sum(complete.cases(task_compare$automation_share_task, task_compare$automation_share_simple))  # occupations compared
sd(task_compare$automation_share_simple, na.rm = TRUE)                                         # spread, for scale
mean(task_compare$automation_share_task - task_compare$automation_share_simple, na.rm = TRUE)  # signed gap

# Well-covered occupations only
ok = task_compare$n_tasks_aei >= 3 & task_compare$importance_covered >= 0.2

sum(ok, na.rm = TRUE)    # how many occupations
cor(task_compare$automation_share_task[ok], task_compare$automation_share_simple[ok], use = "complete.obs")
mean(abs(task_compare$automation_share_task[ok] - task_compare$automation_share_simple[ok]), na.rm = TRUE)
sd(task_compare$automation_share_simple[ok], na.rm = TRUE)
```

# Question 3: How are young people choosing jobs? Look at the % of young people in these top 30 before and after LLM emergence

```{r historic-data}
ddi_historic = read_ipums_ddi("cps_00004.xml")
data_historic = read_ipums_micro(ddi_historic)

data_historic = data_historic %>%
  filter(AGE >= young_min & AGE <= young_max,
         EDUC >= 111,
         EMPSTAT == 1 | EMPSTAT == 10 | EMPSTAT == 12,
         OCC != 0,
         OCC2010 != 9999) %>%
  mutate(EDCYC    = NULL,
         EDDIPGED = NULL,
         EDHGCGED = NULL)

# Exposure
codes_historic = sprintf("%04d", as.integer(data_historic$OCC2010))
data_historic$dv_rating_beta = census_exposure$dv_rating_beta[match(codes_historic, census_exposure$census)]

# Before / after ChatGPT; weights averaged over the years in each period
data_historic = data_historic %>%
  mutate(period = if_else(YEAR <= 2022, "before", "after")) %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  mutate(weight = ASECWT / n_distinct(YEAR)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r historic-shares-by-year}
data_historic$occ_title = as.character(as_factor(data_historic$OCC2010))

# Share of all young graduates in each occupation, within each year
occ_by_year = data_historic %>%
  group_by(YEAR, OCC2010, occ_title) %>%
  summarise(n_people        = n(),
            weighted_people = sum(ASECWT),
            exposure        = first(dv_rating_beta),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(YEAR) %>%
  mutate(share_pct = 100 * weighted_people / sum(weighted_people)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Keep the top 30 occupations from the Question 1 table
occ_top30_by_year = filter(occ_by_year, OCC2010 %in% top30$OCC2010)
```

```{r historic-charts-loop, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
dir.create("occ_charts", showWarnings = FALSE)

occ_list = as.numeric(top30$OCC2010)
occ_top30_by_year$OCC2010 = as.numeric(occ_top30_by_year$OCC2010)

for (i in seq_along(occ_list)) {
  this_code  = occ_list[i]
  this_data  = occ_top30_by_year[occ_top30_by_year$OCC2010 == this_code, ]
  this_title = this_data$occ_title[1]

  p_i = ggplot(this_data, aes(x = YEAR, y = share_pct)) +
    geom_line(color = "navy") +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 2022.5, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(title    = this_title,
         subtitle = paste0("Exposure: ", round(this_data$exposure[1], 2)),
         x = NULL,
         y = "Share of graduates (%)") +
    theme_classic()

  print(p_i)
  ggsave(paste0("occ_charts/", i, "_", this_code, ".png"),
         plot = p_i, width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 150)
}
```

# Question 4: Have outcomes diverged for high-exposure occupations since late 2022? (DiD)

Design: compare the share of young graduates working in high- vs low-exposure occupations before and after 2022 (difference-in-differences), then check the timing with an event study. Needs `occ_table` (Q1), `data_historic` and `top30` already in memory.

## Step 1: exposure groups

```{r q4-groups}
# All occupations with an exposure score, most exposed first
occ_exposure = occ_table %>%
  filter(!is.na(exposure)) %>%
  arrange(desc(exposure))

# Top and bottom third (by number of occupations)
third = round(nrow(occ_exposure) / 3, 0)

occ_top_exposed = head(occ_exposure, third)
occ_low_exposed = tail(occ_exposure, third)

occ_groups = rbind(data.frame(OCC2010 = as.numeric(occ_top_exposed$OCC2010), group = "high"),
                   data.frame(OCC2010 = as.numeric(occ_low_exposed$OCC2010), group = "low"))
```

## Step 2: occupation x year panel

```{r q4-panel}
ids = as.numeric(occ_exposure$OCC2010)
data_historic$OCC2010 = as.numeric(data_historic$OCC2010)

# Total weighted young graduates in each year (the denominator for shares)
year_totals = data_historic %>%
  group_by(YEAR) %>%
  summarise(total_weight = sum(ASECWT), .groups = "drop")

# Weighted headcount for each occupation-year
panel = data_historic %>%
  filter(OCC2010 %in% ids) %>%
  group_by(YEAR, OCC2010) %>%
  summarise(n_people        = n(),
            weighted_people = sum(ASECWT),
            .groups = "drop")

# Fill occupation-years that never appear with 0
panel = panel %>%
  complete(YEAR, OCC2010 = ids,
           fill = list(n_people = 0, weighted_people = 0))

# Shares of all young graduates in that year
panel = panel %>%
  left_join(year_totals, by = "YEAR")
panel$share_pct = 100 * panel$weighted_people / panel$total_weight

# Exposure, group, and before/after indicator
panel$exposure = occ_exposure$exposure[match(panel$OCC2010, ids)]
panel$group    = occ_groups$group[match(panel$OCC2010, occ_groups$OCC2010)]
panel$group[is.na(panel$group)] = "middle"
panel$post     = as.numeric(panel$YEAR > 2022)

# Occupation size before ChatGPT (used as regression weights)
pre_size = panel %>%
  filter(YEAR <= 2022) %>%
  group_by(OCC2010) %>%
  summarise(pre_size = mean(weighted_people), .groups = "drop")

panel = left_join(panel, pre_size, by = "OCC2010")

panel$high       = as.numeric(panel$group == "high")
panel$log_people = log(panel$weighted_people + 1)
panel$exposure10 = panel$exposure * 10   # coefficient = effect per 0.1 of exposure

# High vs low only (the middle third is dropped)
did_data = filter(panel, group %in% c("high", "low"))

# Checks
nrow(panel) == length(ids) * n_distinct(panel$YEAR)   # TRUE = balanced panel
"pre_size" %in% names(did_data)                       # TRUE
```

## Step 3: high vs low over time

```{r q4-plots}
group_year = panel %>%
  filter(group %in% c("high", "low")) %>%
  group_by(YEAR, group) %>%
  summarise(share_pct       = sum(share_pct),
            weighted_people = sum(weighted_people),
            .groups = "drop")

# Index to 2022 = 100 (within each group)
base_2022 = group_year %>%
  filter(YEAR == 2022) %>%
  select(group, base_share = share_pct, base_people = weighted_people)

group_year = left_join(group_year, base_2022, by = "group")

group_year$share_index  = 100 * group_year$share_pct / group_year$base_share
group_year$people_index = 100 * group_year$weighted_people / group_year$base_people

group_colors2 = c(high = "navy", low = "skyblue")

# Chart 1: raw share of young graduates
p_share = ggplot(group_year, aes(x = YEAR, y = share_pct, color = group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2022.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(values = group_colors2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(group_year$YEAR))) +
  labs(title = "Share of young graduates in high- vs low-exposure occupations",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Share of 22-25 graduates (%)",
       color = "Exposure group") +
  theme_classic()

# Chart 2: indexed to 2022 = 100
p_index = ggplot(group_year, aes(x = YEAR, y = share_index, color = group)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, color = "grey70") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2022.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(values = group_colors2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(group_year$YEAR))) +
  labs(title = "Same series, indexed (2022 = 100)",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Index (2022 = 100)",
       color = "Exposure group") +
  theme_classic()

ggsave("high_vs_low_share.png", plot = p_share, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 200)
ggsave("high_vs_low_index.png", plot = p_index, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 200)

p_share
p_index
```

## Step 4: difference-in-differences

```{r q4-did}
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1. Share (percentage points)
m1 = lm(share_pct ~ high:post + factor(OCC2010) + factor(YEAR),
        data = did_data, weights = pre_size)

# 2. Log headcount
m2 = lm(log_people ~ high:post + factor(OCC2010) + factor(YEAR),
        data = did_data, weights = pre_size)

# 3. Continuous exposure, all occupations
m3 = lm(share_pct ~ exposure10:post + factor(OCC2010) + factor(YEAR),
        data = panel, weights = pre_size)

# 4. Drop the COVID years
did_nocovid = filter(did_data, !YEAR %in% c(2020, 2021))
m4 = lm(share_pct ~ high:post + factor(OCC2010) + factor(YEAR),
        data = did_nocovid, weights = pre_size)

# 5. Log headcount again, only occupations with people in every year
always_present = panel %>%
  group_by(OCC2010) %>%
  summarise(min_people = min(weighted_people), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(min_people > 0)

did_present = filter(did_data, OCC2010 %in% always_present$OCC2010)
m5 = lm(log_people ~ high:post + factor(OCC2010) + factor(YEAR),
        data = did_present, weights = pre_size)

# Standard errors clustered by occupation, DiD term only
coeftest(m1, vcov = vcovCL, cluster = did_data$OCC2010)["high:post", ]
coeftest(m2, vcov = vcovCL, cluster = did_data$OCC2010)["high:post", ]
coeftest(m3, vcov = vcovCL, cluster = panel$OCC2010)["exposure10:post", ]
coeftest(m4, vcov = vcovCL, cluster = did_nocovid$OCC2010)["high:post", ]
coeftest(m5, vcov = vcovCL, cluster = did_present$OCC2010)["high:post", ]
```

## Step 5: event study (2022 = base year)

```{r q4-event-study}
years = setdiff(sort(unique(did_data$YEAR)), 2022)

for (y in years) {
  did_data[[paste0("high_", y)]] = did_data$high * (did_data$YEAR == y)
}

f = as.formula(paste("share_pct ~",
                     paste0("high_", years, collapse = " + "),
                     "+ factor(OCC2010) + factor(YEAR)"))

m_event = lm(f, data = did_data, weights = pre_size)

ct = coeftest(m_event, vcov = vcovCL, cluster = did_data$OCC2010)

event_coefs = data.frame(YEAR = as.numeric(sub("high_", "", rownames(ct)[grepl("^high_", rownames(ct))])),
                         est  = ct[grepl("^high_", rownames(ct)), "Estimate"],
                         se   = ct[grepl("^high_", rownames(ct)), "Std. Error"],
                         p    = ct[grepl("^high_", rownames(ct)), "Pr(>|t|)"])
event_coefs

# Add the base year (0 by construction) and plot with 95% intervals
event_plot = rbind(event_coefs, data.frame(YEAR = 2022, est = 0, se = 0, p = NA))
event_plot$lo = event_plot$est - 1.96 * event_plot$se
event_plot$hi = event_plot$est + 1.96 * event_plot$se

p_event = ggplot(event_plot, aes(x = YEAR, y = est)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2022.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), color = "navy") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(event_plot$YEAR))) +
  labs(title = "Event study: high- vs low-exposure occupations",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Difference in share (pp), relative to 2022") +
  theme_classic()

ggsave("event_study.png", plot = p_event, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 200)
p_event
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Summary and limitations

- Employed 22-25 year old graduates work in occupations with an average exposure of 0.43, similar to 30-55 year old graduates (0.45).
- About half of that exposure is automation-style Claude usage and half is augmentation-style.
- Since late 2022 (release of ChatGPT), there is no clear shift in the share of young graduates working in high vs low-exposure occupations.

**Limitations**

- AEI covers only about 10% of O*NET tasks and measures Claude usage, not the share of a job made of AI tasks.
- Exposure and AEI describe occupations, not seniority within an occupation, so entry-level tasks cannot be separated from senior ones.
- The sample is employed graduates only, so changes in hiring or unemployment do not show up in occupation shares. It would be worth exploring hiring and unemployment data as well to see if there are changes in the share of occupations for new hires and unemployment.
- Only 22-25 and 30-55 year old graduates are compared; non-graduates are not included, and older recent university graduates not included.
- Yearly CPS ASEC samples are small, so confidence intervals are wide and moderate effects cannot be ruled out.
